frank (Docs): quick heads-up  PR #1203 adds a C# snippet and a short section on prefetch/eviction to the Optimize toolkit. spotted a few issues during review: the C# example uses the old sync helper, TTL guidance is missing, and the quant table mentions q5_0 (experimental) but no caveats. can eng/runtime/ML sanity-check?
yasmin (Eng): paste the C# snippet + the YAML cell and i'll run it in the examples app.
frank (Docs): C# snippet in PR: 
```csharp
// current (stale) snippet in PR
var resp = client.GenerateSync("redwood/fast-ggml", prompt, maxTokens:256);
Console.WriteLine(resp.Text);
```
YAML quant note in PR: 
```yaml
quant_profile: q5_0
recommendation: experimental, use with caution
```
oli (Runtime): GenerateSync was removed in SDK v2. Use the async pattern `await client.GenerateAsync(...)` or batch helpers for multi-input. For prefetch TTL the SDK supports `client.Cache.Prefetch(prefixes, ttlMs: 600000)` and `client.Cache.Invalidate(prefix)` to evict. Add a callout: prefetching many unique prefixes increases memory; choose TTLs that match prefix churn. Also for per-route low-latency policies recommend `maxBatchLatencyMs: 20` for chat-like short seq workloads.
sara (ML): on q5_0: it's experimental; good to mention current CI coverage is limited. Suggest changing phrasing to: "q5_0: experimental lower-memory profile; run the micro-eval harness below before adopting" and include a tiny eval script suggestion: 200 generation prompts (seeded) + 1k embedding pairs for drift.
yasmin (Eng): here's the minimal C# async replacement i'm testing locally: 
```csharp
// replacement (async) example
var resp = await client.GenerateAsync(new GenerateRequest { Model = "redwood/fast-ggml", Prompt = prompt, MaxTokens = 256 });
Console.WriteLine(resp.Text);
```
plus a C# prefetch example: 
```csharp
// prefetch with ttl
await client.Cache.PrefetchAsync(new []{"session_prefix_v1"}, ttlMs: 600000);
var resp = await client.GenerateAsync(...);
```
lint-bot: docs-link-check: broken link in PR #1203 -> /docs/sdk/csharp/GenerateSync (404) :warning:
frank (Docs): perfect, yasmin. i'll replace the snippet and add the TTL + invalidate examples. sara, can you paste the micro-eval harness pseudo-code you recommend so i can include it as a footnote?
sara (ML): micro-eval suggestion (pseudo): 
```bash
# pseudo-harness
python eval_quant.py --model redwood/fast-ggml --profiles [q4_1,q5_0] \n  --gen-samples 200 --embed-pairs 1000 --seed 42 --report results.md
```
add guidance: "if generation bleu/rouge drops > X or embedding cosine drift > Y, do not switch" (we'll put thresholds in the notebook). also note q4_1 may be preferable for instruction-following tasks.
oli (Runtime): small extra: add a migration checklist bullet: "search repo for GenerateSync, batch.create, prefill, batch.send" and recommend replacing with `GenerateAsync`, `client.batch.request`, and `client.cache.prefetch`. also add a short callout under batching: "multimodal inputs may require smaller max_batch_size or dedicated image routes".
frank (Docs): great. i'll update the PR with the C# async + prefetch + invalidate examples, soften the q5_0 language and include sara's micro-eval snippet + link to the quant-eval notebook. also fixing the broken link target. opened PR #1204 with the tiny replacements.
ci-bot: PR #1204 created by @frank  docs-lint found one minor style nit (code-block language tag), fixed automatically, link-check passed :white_check_mark:
yasmin (Eng): quick LGTM on the snippet changes. merging after frank updates the changelog blurb.
frank (Docs): merged and added changelog entry: "Optimize: C# SDK snippets updated for SDK-v2; added KV prefetch TTL/invalidate guidance; softened q5_0 recommendation and included micro-eval harness." closing thread. :tada:
